proposals.name: Ch. 9, Theorem 9.12 (Hodge theorem) and Theorem 9.13: $H^1_{DR}(X)=\Omega(X)\oplus\bar\Omega(X)$ and the $(1,1)$-form image of the Laplacian
proposals.proposed_evidence: McMullen printed pp.88–89 states the scalar de Rham harmonic-class theorem and the top-degree Laplacian integral criterion. The proof explicitly obtains surjectivity from arithmetic genus=topological genus via Corollary9.11 and uses the residue map on H1,1 for Theorem9.13. The approved Hodge A inventory instead establishes the arbitrary-line-bundle Dolbeault complex and harmonic representatives in degrees (0,0),(0,1); these are proved in the local Hodge decomposition and corollary without importing the scalar de Rham claim. Plan order1612 divisors-riemann-roch-and-duality is a later consumer of Hodge order1610, and its structure-sheaf/genus, comparison, residue and RR machinery is the correct topic destination for this source route. This is a scope deferral, not an assertion that either exact scalar de Rham theorem has already been authored at the destination.

proposals.name: Ch. 6, Theorem 6.11: a 1-form on a compact Riemann surface is harmonic iff it is closed and norm-minimising in its cohomology class
proposals.proposed_evidence: McMullen printed p.61 Theorem6.11 characterizes a scalar real/complex one-form by closedness and formal norm minimization in its de Rham class, then invokes general elliptic theory for attainment. The batch9 claim inventory is the smooth Dolbeault quotient for arbitrary holomorphic Hermitian line bundles, whose degree-one forms are automatically Dolbeault-closed; it neither promises nor uses minimization in de Rham classes. Local Hodge step4.1 and corollary step2.1 prove the required Dolbeault uniqueness by orthogonality. No norm-minimization supplier is cited in those arguments or the five exact B computations. The out-of-scope disposition therefore preserves the approved bundle Dolbeault subject without deleting an approved claim.

proposals.name: Ch. 6, Theorem 6.13 (Hodge): $H^k(M)\cong H^k_{DR}(M)$ for a compact Riemannian manifold
proposals.proposed_evidence: McMullen printed p.66 Theorem6.13 is the general compact Riemannian-manifold de Rham Hodge isomorphism in every k, followed by real de Rham adjoints and the full smooth de Rham splitting. The fixed Hodge page order1610 is restricted to a compact Riemann surface and line-bundle-valued (0,q) Dolbeault theory for q=0,1. Its local operator and Hodge items explicitly prove these two Dolbeault degrees instead of assuming this general theorem. Thus the all-dimension/all-degree scalar de Rham result is outside the approved inventory and not an unmet prerequisite of the authored claim.

proposals.name: Ch. 14, Corollary 14.3: existence of a meromorphic section of $L$ with a pole of degree at most $1+h^1(L)$ at a prescribed point
proposals.proposed_evidence: McMullen printed p.119 Corollary14.3 promises a nonzero meromorphic section of an arbitrary holomorphic line bundle with its sole permitted pole at a supplied point and pole order at most1+h1(L). The Hodge page defines meromorphic sections and proves finite-dimensional smooth Dolbeault groups; it does not promise existence or prescribe poles. The target divisors-riemann-roch-and-duality order1612 depends on Hodge and carries divisor-associated bundles, point-divisor exact sequences, cohomology comparison, RR and prescribed-principal-parts material. That is the appropriate topic routing for pole construction, so the scope deferral can stand. Exact limitation: the current target inventory does not itself contain a theorem with this arbitrary-line-bundle bound; accepting the decline must not falsely certify that exact source corollary as already delivered.

proposals.name: Ch. 11, Theorem 11.1 (Serre duality $H^1(X,\mathcal O_{-D})^\ast\cong\Omega_D(X)$) and Theorem 11.2 (Riemann-Roch)
proposals.proposed_evidence: McMullen printed p.94 states divisor/sheaf Serre duality H1(O_-D)*=Omega_D and the final divisor RR dimension formula, with the canonical product into H1(Omega). The Hodge page already proves only its approved harmonic integral duality H0,1(E)*=H0(K tensor E*) from smooth representatives and star, with no implicit sheaf comparison. The later planned divisors-riemann-roch-and-duality page order1612 explicitly contains thm-cech-dolbeault-comparison-for-line-bundles-on-compact-surfaces, thm-serre-duality-compact-riemann-surfaces and thm-riemann-roch-compact-riemann-surfaces. Thus both exact source topics are concretely assigned to the destination while the producer retains the analytic supplier those proofs consume.

proposals.name: Ch. VI §6.2, (6.8): the full commutation relations on a hermitian manifold and the torsion operator $\tau=[\Lambda,d'\omega]$
proposals.proposed_evidence: Demailly Ch.VI §6.2 printed pp.306–309 gives the general Hermitian torsion operator tau=[Lambda,d-prime omega] and four corrected Lefschetz commutation identities. Its proof compares first-order adjoints under a metric Taylor expansion. The approved compact-curve bundle Dolbeault page uses neither the general Lefschetz operators nor those four identities: local-formula steps2.1–4.2 compute the weighted adjoint and each Laplacian directly, and harmonic-star-duality step2.1 directly computes the full dual-bundle commutation with metric weight2/(rho psi). On a curve d-prime omega has type(2,1) and vanishes for dimension reasons, so the general torsion correction machinery adds no missing local result. The general Hermitian-manifold calculus is outside this page inventory; the source row should stand without importing an unproved general commutator theorem.
